# Results Summary (generated by 09_make_summary.py from results/*.csv)

Seed = 42. "Grouped CV" = 5-fold StratifiedGroupKFold by Order Id.
Do not edit by hand: re-run `python 09_make_summary.py`.

## Headline numbers

**DataCo inflation decomposition (XGBoost, A2)**
- Paper single split replicated: 0.9330
- S0 as submitted (row CV): 0.9288 ± 0.0031
- S1 without Order Status: 0.9134 ± 0.0057
- S2 without shipping date: 0.8293 ± 0.0030
- S3 without order-date string / PII: 0.7999 ± 0.0018
- S4 + grouped CV: 0.7365 ± 0.0032
- S5 clean feature set, grouped CV: 0.7670 ± 0.0034
- Control (+ parsed ship-minus-order days): 0.9903 ± 0.0006

**Random forest discrepancy (A3)**
- RF(200, depth 15, balanced), single split: 0.8878
- RF(100, unlimited), 5-fold row CV: 0.9608 ± 0.0029
- Same RF(100), grouped CV: 0.7810 ± 0.0035

**IoT audit**
- DS2 permutation test: observed 0.4893, null mean 0.4988 (SD 0.0231), p = 0.6617
- Fused RF, single split: 0.9492; 5-fold: 0.9481
- dataset_source only: 0.8636; source + speed: 0.9308
- Within DS2 rows: 0.5078; within DS3 rows: 1.0000
- K-Means vs source file: 0.9529 (ARI); silhouette 0.4119

**Corrected DataCo benchmark (grouped 5-fold, ROC-AUC mean of folds, C2)**
- XGBoost 0.7681 ± 0.0058; Random Forest 0.7673 ± 0.0038; MLP 0.7610 ± 0.0052; Logistic Regression 0.7426 ± 0.0041; Shipping Mode only 0.7282 ± 0.0040

**Lookup table vs ML (pooled out-of-fold ROC-AUC, C11/C13)**
- 4-cell mode lookup, out-of-fold: 0.7249
- 8-cell mode x noon lookup, out-of-fold: 0.7569
- 32-cell lookup in-sample / out-of-fold: 0.7739 / 0.7716
- XGBoost / Random Forest out-of-fold: 0.7680 / 0.7671
- Order-level bootstrap, XGBoost minus 32-cell lookup: -0.0037 (95% CI -0.0061 to -0.0012)
- Order-level bootstrap, Random Forest minus 32-cell lookup: -0.0046 (95% CI -0.007 to -0.0022)

**Temporal hold-out (C5, ROC-AUC):** Shipping Mode only (LR) 0.7341; Logistic Regression 0.7471; Random Forest 0.7759; XGBoost 0.7767; MLP (feed-forward NN) 0.7680

## Caveats to state in the paper

1. The XGBoost and MLP grids used a 60,000-row sample that overlaps the outer folds;
   they are sensitivity analyses, not nested tuning.
2. DeLong tests treat order items as independent; items of one order share a label,
   so very small p-values are overstated. C13 uses an order-level bootstrap instead.
3. The audit covers three public files only and does not describe IoT logistics data
   in general.

### A1: DataCo leakage tests (`A1_dataco_leakage_tests.csv`)

| Column | Test | Result | Implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery Status | Late delivery <=> target = 1 | 1.0000 | Identical to target |
| Days for shipping (real) | rule: real > scheduled reproduces target | 0.9755 | Target is defined from it |
| shipping date (DateOrders) | shipping date - order date == real shipping days | 0.9742 | Rebuilds the removed leakage column |
| shipping date (DateOrders) | rule: (ship - order) > scheduled reproduces target | 0.9519 | Post-event |
| Order Status | share of CANCELED / SUSPECTED_FRAUD rows labelled late | 0.0000 (n=7,754) | Post-event outcome; 0% late by construction |
| Order Id | orders whose items all share one label | 1.0000 | Row-level split puts items of the same order in train and test |
| Order Id | mean items (rows) per order | 2.75 | Needs group-aware CV |
